## YOUR TASK

Build three production deliverables for Phase 3 of the AI-driven UI/UX design pipeline:

### Deliverable 1 — "Design Spec Importer" Figma Plugin (`mcp-figma/plugin/`)
A TypeScript Figma Plugin (~300–500 lines) that reads a `design_spec.json` file and creates a complete Figma design inside an open Figma file. The plugin must:

1. **Page creation** — Call `figma.createPage()` for each screen defined in `design_spec.screens[]`
2. **Frame creation** — Call `figma.createFrame()` with exact `width` and `height` from spec for each screen's frame
3. **Auto-layout setup** — Set `node.layoutMode`, `node.itemSpacing`, `node.paddingTop/Bottom/Left/Right`, `node.primaryAxisAlignItems`, `node.counterAxisAlignItems` from spec layout properties
4. **Component creation** — Call `figma.createComponent()` for each entry in `design_spec.components[]`
5. **Variant creation** — Call `figma.combineAsVariants()` for components with `variants[]` arrays, generating full variant sets from Cartesian product
6. **Visual properties** — Set `node.fills`, `node.fontName`, `node.fontSize`, `node.fontWeight`, `node.effects` from design system `typography` and `colors` in spec
7. **Design token variables** — Call `figma.variables.createVariableCollection()` and `figma.variables.createVariable()` for all entries in `design_spec.design_system.colors`, `typography`, and `spacing`
8. **Token binding** — Call `node.setBoundVariable()` to bind token variables to corresponding component properties
9. **Implementation comments** — Add per-frame comments referencing FR coverage (`screen.fr_coverage[]`) using `figma.activeFile.comments` or the plugin comment API
10. **FR mapping output** — After creation, display a summary in the plugin UI: which FRs map to which frames + node IDs

Plugin project structure:
```
mcp-figma/plugin/
  manifest.json           ← Figma plugin manifest (name, id, api, main, ui, editorType)
  package.json            ← devDependencies: @figma/plugin-typings, typescript, esbuild
  tsconfig.json           ← target: ES2017, lib: ["es2017"], module: CommonJS, strict: true
  esbuild.config.js       ← bundles src/code.ts → dist/code.js (single file, no external deps)
  src/
    code.ts               ← Main plugin logic (runs in Figma sandbox, no DOM access)
    ui.html               ← Plugin UI iframe (file picker, progress display, error reporting)
    types.ts              ← TypeScript interfaces for DesignSpec, Screen, Component, DesignSystem
    schema.ts             ← JSON Schema validation for design_spec.json (runtime check)
    builders/
      page-builder.ts     ← figma.createPage() orchestration
      frame-builder.ts    ← figma.createFrame() + auto-layout wiring
      component-builder.ts← figma.createComponent() + figma.combineAsVariants()
      token-builder.ts    ← figma.variables.* API calls
      comment-builder.ts  ← FR comment injection
  dist/                   ← esbuild output (gitignored)
  tests/
    code.test.ts          ← Unit tests (vitest + @figma/plugin-ds mock)
    integration/
      plugin.spec.ts      ← Integration tests with Figma Plugin runner
```

### Deliverable 4 — `design_spec.json` JSON Schema (`plugin/schema/design_spec.schema.json`)
A JSON Schema Draft-07 document that formally validates all `design_spec.json` files before the plugin executes. Must cover:
- `project` (string, required)
- `design_system.colors` (object, required, pattern: `^#[0-9A-Fa-f]{6}$`)
- `design_system.typography` (object of font-family/fontSize/fontWeight objects)
- `design_system.spacing` (array of numbers)
- `screens[]` (array — name, fr_coverage[], width, height, components[])
- `components[]` (array — name, variants[], layout, padding object)
- Additional properties: false (strict — no unknown fields)

**ARCHITECTURE DECISIONS (from Phase 2 JOINT APPROVED blueprint):**

```
ADR-1: Plugin Location
  Chosen:    mcp-figma/plugin/ (co-located with MCP server)
  Why:       Shared TypeScript type definitions for DesignSpec; single repo simplifies token schema updates;
             plugin and MCP server versioned together
  Rejected:
    Separate repo — double maintenance burden; type drift between plugin input and MCP server output
    Global library — not a reusable skill; tightly coupled to mcp-figma server

ADR-2: Build Tooling
  Chosen:    esbuild (single-file bundle to dist/code.js)
  Why:       Figma requires exactly one JS file; esbuild 10x faster than webpack;
             TypeScript supported natively; zero config for basic plugin bundles
  Rejected:
    webpack — 10x slower for this use case; config complexity not warranted for 300-500 line codebase
    rollup — slower than esbuild; more config required for TypeScript + plugin sandbox

ADR-3: Design Spec Validation
  Chosen:    JSON Schema Draft-07 validated at plugin startup (before any figma.* API calls)
  Why:       Fail-fast prevents partial Figma file creation; JSON Schema is language-agnostic
             (AI agents can validate output before handing to user); Draft-07 supported by all JSON
             Schema validators
  Rejected:
    Zod — adds runtime dependency; Figma plugin bundle must be minimal (no node_modules in dist)
    Manual validation — error-prone; doesn't generate useful error messages for AI agents

ADR-4: State Management
  Chosen:    useSyncedState (Figma Plugin API) for multi-user coordination
  Why:       Native CRDT support; persists across plugin closes; no custom sync layer needed;
             multi-user Figma files require CRDT-safe state
  Rejected:
    figma.clientStorage — not shared across users; wrong for multi-user design sessions
    Custom CRDT — unnecessary complexity when Figma API provides it natively

ADR-5: Testing Strategy
  Chosen:    vitest + @figma/plugin-ds mock for unit; Figma Plugin runner for integration
  Why:       vitest runs in Node.js without Figma app; @figma/plugin-ds provides full
             figma.* API mock surface; integration tests verify real plugin execution
  Rejected:
    Jest — slower; ESM interop friction with TypeScript; vitest is drop-in compatible
    No unit tests — Figma sandbox makes debugging hard; unit coverage is essential safety net

ADR-6: design_spec.json AI Provenance
  Chosen:    Required `_metadata.generated_by` field (AI agent name + model + timestamp)
  Why:       MeitY AI Advisory 2023 compliance; enables traceability of AI-generated design decisions;
             consensus-agent uses this to validate spec authenticity
  Rejected:
    No provenance — non-compliant with MeitY AI Advisory 2023; no audit trail

ADR-7: Accessibility Validation
  Chosen:    mcp-figma compute_apca_contrast + compute_wcag_contrast called via MCP in Phase 3.5
  Why:       Tools already exist in mcp-figma (RS=1.0); APCA v0.0.98G coefficients verified;
             WCAG 2.1 ratio computation correct; no need to re-implement in plugin
  Rejected:
    Plugin-side accessibility check — adds bundle size; mcp-figma already has verified implementations
    Manual check — not automatable; cannot gate DESIGN APPROVED verdict on manual review
```
